# Arca Swift SDK

Native Swift concurrency SDK. See README.md and the public Swift SDK reference
for the full API. Use canonical market IDs (for example hl:0:BTC), keep monetary
values as decimal strings, and preserve server authority for execution/risk.
Public source preference is optional and reversible; Arca remains the default.

## Aggregation watches and reconnects (2.12.1)

`watchAggregation` creates its watch on the socket (`create_aggregation_watch`),
not over REST. The server destroys that watch with the connection, so the SDK
re-creates it after every reconnect or rotation; the stream keeps its last value
meanwhile and retries a failed re-create with backoff. Once a connection has
authenticated, a server error rejects one request (a non-canonical market id, a
path outside the credential's scope) and never closes the socket; an error that
names a `requestId` fails only that request. The
reconnect backoff (1 s doubling to 30 s) resets only after a connection has
stayed up for 30 s, `ensureConnected()` does not cut a pending backoff short, and
returning to the foreground reconnects at once without resetting the backoff.

## Market data diagnostics (2.12.0)

`watchMarketDataDiagnostics()` observes a conflated cumulative `MarketDataDiagnostics`
snapshot: Swift returns an AsyncStream (await it); Kotlin returns a StateFlow.
`marketDataDiagnostics` reads the current snapshot (await in Swift). Observation
adds no socket, subscription or polling timer. Updates accompany traffic at most
once a second plus source/interest/connection transitions. Cancel observation to
release it. Use foreground-window deltas, not number of diagnostic callbacks.

Fields: elapsedMs, preference, requestedPriceMarkets, directSubscriptions,
arcaServingMarkets/hyperliquidServingMarkets (last routed quote source),
arcaPriceValues/hyperliquidPriceValues, arcaCandleFrames/hyperliquidCandleFrames,
hyperliquidFailures/hyperliquidRecoveries/hyperliquidRecoveryMs,
arcaConnected/arcaDisconnects, arcaPayloadBytes/hyperliquidPayloadBytes, firstPriceMs.
Counters last for one SDK client and include reconnects. Deliberate disconnects
can increment Arca disconnects; split lifecycle windows. Intentional suspension
cancels a pending direct-recovery duration. All bytes are incoming application
payloads, excluding framing/TLS; Arca's count includes its shared account socket.
The first price delay starts at socket-manager creation and concerns the first
routed interested price. It is not venue latency. Quiet prices are not failures,
no exchange timestamp is invented, and Arca still owns finalized candles.

## Wallet snapshot and money figures (2.14.0)

`walletSnapshot(ownerAddress:arcaPath:boundaryId:)` reads the schema-2 wallet
snapshot (`WalletSnapshot`): Cash, every trading account under the owner's
root, the money moving between them (`moving`), the funding operations and
`totals`, composed by Arca at one journal position so
`totals.totalMicro = cashMicro + movingMicro + tradingMicro` in every frame
(an empty `boundaryId` names a pre-Cash wallet). `walletSnapshotEvents(...)`
streams it (`AsyncThrowingStream<WalletSnapshot, Error>`) with the same
resume and backoff as `walletAccountEvents`, keyed on `watermark.sequence`.

`watchWalletMoney(ownerAddress:arcaPath:boundaryId:)` returns a
`WalletMoneyWatchStream` whose `money` is the latest `WalletMoney`: a
`MoneyFigure` for the total, for Cash and for each account (`accounts`,
`orderedAccounts`), each one Arca's figure VERBATIM (`settledMicro`: Cash
`confirmedMicro`, an account's `balances.totalMicro`, `totals.totalMicro`;
`availableMicro`: Cash `availableMicro`, an account's `withdrawableMicro`)
plus the legs of the operations moving money into or out of it (`arriving`,
`departing`: one `MoneyLeg` per operation with `stage` reserved / inTransit /
expected, `amountMicro`, `counterparty` cash / account / external / unknown).
Rules, all from the frame: a `reserved` leg shows at both ends; an `inTransit`
leg at its destination when listed, else at its source (a send); `expected`
only at its destination and never in `arrivingMicro` or `inMotion`; the total
carries only legs that cross the wallet (deposits, sends; also Cash's own
sends in `cash.operations` and `pendingInMicro`); a leg whose other end the
frame does not list still renders on the visible end. NOTHING is summed into
a figure on the client; `arrivingMicro`/`departingMicro`/`expectedMicro` are
caption totals only. One frame, one value: every figure carries the same
`watermark`; hold one watch per wallet and render it everywhere. The only
gates are another owner/root/realm or an older `watermark.sequence`
(ignored) and an unknown schema (refused); a `totals` mismatch is a
`diagnostics` entry, never a gate. `predict(_:)` adds only the legs of an
accepted operation (`MoneyPrediction`: requestId, amount, from, to) until the
frame that carries it, never moving a figure. `revalue(_:)` takes a venue
frame (`MoneyRevaluation(arcaId:exchangeState:)`) and sets `revaluedMicro`
verbatim only when it is newer than the figure's `asOf` and the frame lists no
settlement toward the account (`heldBy` empty, no incoming leg in motion);
`settledMicro` never moves with it. `change` names the operation or the venue
that moved a figure with a signed `deltaMicro` caption, only when the frame
makes it attributable. Contract: documents/contracts/sdk-money-figure.md;
fixtures shared by all four SDKs:
backend/libs/arca-go/fundingv9/testdata/wallet-money/.

## Scoped projection watches and interest-scoped mids (2.13.0)

`watchProjection(name:paths:prefix:exchange:)` watches a registered projection
for the accounts named: `paths` (max 500 exact object paths) and/or a `prefix`
sub-tree, both intersected with the projection's registered resources (a path
outside them is dropped; they compose as AND). The server reply is the scope's
snapshot (a path set whole; a prefix scope's first page, the rest fetched over
REST with the same prefix). `setPaths(_:)` / `setPrefix(_:)` replace the scope
in place under the same watch id (`update_projection_watch`; the ack carries the
new scope's snapshot, which replaces the rows; a later call supersedes an
earlier one); `scope` is the current interest set. A watch with no `paths` and
no `prefix` is EMPTY — it delivers nothing until `setPaths` names a set — and
never means every covered account; a client that wants the whole projection
passes the projection's own prefix (on a realm-wide projection, the shape to
avoid on a device). Frames are per-account deltas (`removed` drops rows); the
stream re-marks rows against mids between deltas, subscribing to mids only for
the markets its rows hold; reconnects and rotations re-create the watch with
the current scope. Requires `arca:ReadProjection` on the projection name.
`getProjectionValuations(name:prefix:path:paths:cursor:limit:)` is the REST read
with the same narrowing.

`watchPrices(exchange:markets:)`: the market list is the stream's price interest
on BOTH providers. The direct Hyperliquid source subscribes one `bbo` per market;
the Arca socket's `subscribe_mids` carries the union of every live consumer's
markets (`watchPrices`, `watchExchangeState`, `watchObject`, `watchAggregation`,
`watchProjection` all declare the markets their positions hold), is re-sent when
the union changes (widening at once, narrowing after the release debounce) and
is replayed on reconnect. `setMarkets` changes a stream's set in place. Only an
unscoped `watchPrices()` (empty list) asks the server for every market. A market
no earlier consumer asked for is not in the retained snapshot yet; it lands with
the snapshot the widened subscription triggers, one round trip after return.
Driving the manager directly: `acquireMids(exchange:allMarkets:)` /
`releaseMids(allMarkets:)` are the refcounts (default `true` keeps the old
all-markets meaning); a bare `subscribeMids` / `unsubscribeMids` pair is left
alone by them. Measured from 2026-10-17 02:32 UTC on production (payload
bytes, 5 min): one market 0.02 KiB/s, a 22-market board 1.1 KiB/s (7.8
frames/s), every market (567 ids) 6.2 KiB/s, versus Hyperliquid `bbo` on the
same 22 markets 7.8 KiB/s (57 frames/s) and `allMids` 4.8 KiB/s;
`marketDataDiagnostics` reports `arcaPayloadBytes` / `hyperliquidPayloadBytes`
per client.

## Prioritized public quotes (2.15.0)

MarketDataBudget / setMarketDataBudget is opt-in; nil/null restores legacy BBO routing.
Higher priorities use canonical market IDs, merged by the builder from visible consumers.
Interests remain owned by existing watchPrices, account, valuation and sizing watches.
Budget payload bytes/second and receive messages/second independently; message count is
only a device-work proxy. Coarse allMids coverage may exceed a too-small budget. Candles,
Arca fallback, TLS and other app traffic are outside this quote target.
One allMids per needed DEX plus selected BBO, or BBO-only when cheaper and both targets fit.
Ten-second received-frame cost windows, slow cost decreases and retained-selection tie
preference stabilize the plan. Builders should delay device/network budget upgrades.
allMids has no venue timestamp, and a received BBO remains preferred even when quiet.
One canonical batch per coarse frame; server-priced money/execution authority is unchanged.

await arca.setMarketDataBudget(.init(bytesPerSecond: 10_000, messagesPerSecond: 12,
    priorities: ["hl:0:BTC": 100, "hl:1:TSLA": 60]))
// Pass nil to restore the default BBO policy.
await arca.setMarketDataBudget(nil)

## Bounded native price calculations (2.15.0)

`ws.midsEvents()` emits full merged price snapshots, with one newest pending
snapshot per consumer. Merge happens before conflation: sparse updates for
separate assets cannot erase each other's latest prices. Equal-price received
observations remain observable when the low-level consumer keeps up; public
`watchPrices.updates` still skips unchanged maps. Intermediate ticks may be
skipped under load. Unsubscription clears replay for a new subscription lifetime.
Price-driven `watchExchangeState` revaluation uses immutable captured inputs and
rejects results after structural epoch changes or stop. `watchMaxOrderSize` local
derivation uses one background worker plus one newest pending input, preserving
progress during sustained arrivals. Structural acceptance and price publication
share an epoch fence; server-priced sizing remains server authoritative. Swift
`watchPrices.stop()` also ends its private updates worker. Kotlin exchange-watch
startup and initial local sizing derivation explicitly use Dispatchers.Default.
Order/fill events, critical state transitions and authoritative reconciliation are
not routed through the replaceable calculation queue. This bounds the selected
price calculation paths, not every SDK event stream or UI/GPU work. Render the
last completed snapshot; never await a new calculation during a UI render.
